root_idea.summary: The root is oriented toward elevation, rising, and forceful upward movement.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop meanings of leaping or surging, eminence and structural tiers, ascent over a wall, and the Qur’anic sūrah as a distinct elevated or bounded section. The bracelet and Persian-leader terms are reported as Arabicized borrowings rather than as straightforward native developments of the root.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form V verb has a distinct wall-scaling use and is normalized to the perfect-tense dictionary citation form.
The Quranic plural is presented under the supported singular citation form سِوَارٌ.
This is a distinct Quran-attested noun meaning a wall.
This is a distinct Quran-attested noun meaning a Qur’anic chapter or section.

senses.definition: To climb or scale a wall, including climbing over it to gain access.
senses.usage_conditions: Quran-attested Form V usage describing ascent over a wall; the associated construction may use the wall as the object or refer to climbing upon its wall.

senses.definition: A bracelet or armlet worn as adornment.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural أَسَاوِرُ. In the supplied Quran-focused discussion, أَسْوِرَةٌ is associated with gold in 43:53, while أَسَاوِرُ is used for silver in 76:21; this is a contextual usage distinction, not a different basic object.
In its Quranic occurrence, the word denotes a separating wall or barrier.

senses.definition: A distinct chapter or section of the Qur’an.
senses.usage_conditions: The Qur’anic term presents each sūrah as a bounded unit of revelation, a distinct degree or section within the whole, sometimes explained by comparison with a city wall or with an elevated degree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leap or spring toward or upon someone; to assault or assail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may describe a direct attack or an aggressive leap, including the conventional image of an intoxicated drinking companion assaulting another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rush, rise, or circulate into the head; to have an overpowering effect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially said of wine or the force of a cup mounting into the drinker’s head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become angry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of forceful rising or assault.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rise, become elevated, or ascend, including ascending a wall; figuratively, to aspire to eminence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The wall-ascent usage and the idiom of rising toward eminence belong to the same elevation branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wall or enclose a city, town, or similar place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causative construction meaning to provide a place with a wall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a bracelet or bracelets upon someone; to deck someone with bracelets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived construction formed from سِوَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual leaping upon one another, assault, or fighting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form III verbal noun describes reciprocal attack; it can also be used figuratively when anxieties or other forces assail a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An overpowering influence on the head, said of speech or language.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use equating forceful impact with something taking hold of the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To climb or ascend and take or seize what has been reached.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical construction recorded alongside wall-scaling, in which ascent is followed by acquisition of the place or object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on a bracelet or bracelets, or deck oneself with them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V reflexive bracelet-related use, distinct from the Quranic wall-scaling use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leaping or springing with or upon another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise or stretch oneself up toward someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic elevation construction comparable to stretching oneself upward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The uppermost part or crown of the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare traditional usage reported with variant interpretations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An entertainment or repast to which guests are invited.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical item reported as Persian and adopted into Arabic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of fig, identified as ficus sur.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name, distinct from the wall meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leap or spring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic nominal action of forceful upward movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A surge, force, or overpowering effect, as of wine, venom, hunger, or joy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may describe something rushing into or taking effect in the head, or an intense movement of emotion or appetite.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A paroxysm or fit of fever.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage for an acute outbreak of fever.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An outburst, fit, or vehemence of anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can denote either the eruption of anger or, by extension, anger itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Impetuousness or ardor, especially the flush of youth or the impetuousness of battle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The domain is supplied by the expression: the term is not restricted to one age group or object class in general.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The coercive force, tyranny, might, or valor of a sultan.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage for the force exerted by political authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vehemence or intensity of cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of severe cold as an intense onset or force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Eminence, nobility, high rank, station, or excellence; also superior or hardy quality in camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical meaning of the headword distinct from its Quranic technical sense of a chapter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A goodly, tall, or elevated structure; a course or row of stones or bricks, or a level of a structure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The structural uses include a tier or degree of a building or wall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremity or limit of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general boundary or terminal-point usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sign or token, especially a mark of glory, honor, dignity, or nobility.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The generic sign meaning and the more specific sign of status are recorded under the same lexical branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One accustomed to spring upon or assault another; an epithet for a dog or a lion because of its leaping attack.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The human use includes an assailant who attacks or insults a drinking companion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One into whose head wine quickly rises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative agent noun based on the rapid upward effect of wine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Speech or language that has an overpowering effect on the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use for forceful or overwhelming speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Height or an elevated degree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in an idiomatic expression for an affection rising to a high degree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Persian leader or horseman, especially one firm and skilled on horseback and in archery.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized Persian title or designation, with reported senses ranging from a great king to a capable mounted fighter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leather pillow or cushion on which one leans or reclines.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is مَسَاوِرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Adorned with a bracelet or bracelets; figuratively, made a king or chief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The political sense is explained as arising from bracelet adornment as a sign of leadership.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where a bracelet is worn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-noun-like use parallel to other formations naming the place of an adornment.

Overpowering effect of speech or language.

Force, tyranny, or might of a sultan.
Eminence, rank, excellence, and a mark of glory are distinct branches stated in one unit.
Rows, courses, and degrees of a structure are covered by the structural-tier meaning.

Bracelet and its Quranic plural forms.
Assaultive epithet applied to a dog.

One rapidly affected by wine rising into the head.
Pointer to the preceding lexical entry.
Bracelet-adorned and figuratively made king or chief.

cautions: Lane's printed Quran reference for the Form V wall-scaling entry uses the historical notation “xxxviii. 20”; the public Quran example follows the independently supplied QAC location 38:21 and does not treat the printed citation as a modern location.

The bracelet vocabulary and إِسْوَارٌ ‘Persian leader or horseman’ are described in the supplied lexical evidence as Arabicized or borrowed terms; their inclusion here does not assert that every such form derives natively from the root’s core semantic principle.
